cards.text: All the people of Judah take Uzziah, son of King Amaziah, and make him king in his father's place. He's SIXTEEN, friend. I've sat in junk drawers longer than this man has been alive.

cards.question: Sixteen-year-old Uzziah sits on the throne in Jerusalem a long time. He reigns for ___ years.

cards.text: After his father Amaziah rests with his fathers, Uzziah rebuilds Eloth and restores it to Judah. Sixteen and renovating a whole town, while I've watched grown bakers lose a fight to a stuck cookie box lid.

cards.question: True or false: young King Uzziah does what is right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.

cards.text: And this young king doesn't figure it all out alone. He seeks God all through the days of a man named Zechariah.

cards.question: Uzziah seeks God all through the days of Zechariah. What does Zechariah do for the young king?

answers.text: Instructs him in the fear of God
Leads his army into every battle
Guards the treasury of the temple

cards.question: Here's the line this whole story hangs on. As long as Uzziah sought the LORD, God gave him ___.

cards.text: Uzziah goes to war against the Philistines and tears down the walls of Gath, Jabneh and Ashdod. That's not a battle, friend, that's a DEMOLITION CREW.

cards.question: After tearing down those Philistine walls, Uzziah ___ cities near Ashdod and among the Philistines.
True or false: Uzziah beats the Philistines, the Arabs in Gur-baal and the Meunites on his own strength alone.

cards.text: The Ammonites start bringing tribute to Uzziah. Meanwhile, word about this king is traveling, and I mean TRAVELING.

cards.question: Uzziah has become exceedingly powerful. How far does his fame spread?

answers.text: As far as the border of Egypt
As far as the land of Assyria
As far as the island of Cyprus

cards.text: Then Uzziah goes on a building spree: towers at Jerusalem's gates, towers in the desert, and many cisterns for all his livestock. He's got farmers and vinedressers in the hills and fertile fields too, because this man is a lover of the soil.

His army runs by divisions: 2,600 family leaders over 307,500 men trained for war, every one supplied with shields, spears, helmets, armor, bows and slingstones. Back in the junk drawer, my whole army was two rubber bands and a dead battery.

cards.question: Back in Jerusalem, Uzziah puts skillfully designed devices on the towers and corners. What are they built to do?

answers.text: Shoot arrows and catapult large stones
Pour hot oil down on attackers
Flash signals to the army far away

cards.question: Uzziah's fame spreads far and wide. According to the text, how does he get so powerful?

answers.text: He took gold from the temple

cards.text: But here's the turn, friend. When Uzziah becomes powerful, his arrogance leads to his own destruction, and he walks right into the temple of the LORD.

cards.question: King Uzziah walks up to the altar of incense in the temple of the LORD. What is he there to do?

answers.text: Pray for the priests serving there
Bring a gift of gold for it

cards.text: Then Azariah the priest goes in after the king. And he does NOT come by himself.

cards.question: Azariah the priest goes into the temple after King Uzziah, along with ___ brave priests of the LORD.

cards.text: They take their stand right in front of King Uzziah. One king, one altar, and a WHOLE ROOM of priests saying not today.

cards.question: The priests tell Uzziah he has no right to offer incense to the LORD. Only the ___ of Aaron are consecrated to burn incense.
True or false: the priests tell Uzziah he will still receive honor from the LORD God for this.

cards.text: Uzziah's standing there with a censer in his hand, and he's ENRAGED, raging at the priests right in the house of the LORD. Friend, when eighty priests tell you to put it down, you PUT IT DOWN.

cards.question: While King Uzziah rages at the priests before the altar of incense, something breaks out on his forehead. What is it?

cards.text: Azariah the chief priest and all the priests turn and look at the king. And there it is, right on his forehead.

cards.question: The priests see the leprosy on Uzziah's forehead and rush him out of the temple. What does Uzziah himself do?

answers.text: He grabs hold of the altar

cards.question: True or false: Uzziah hurries out of the temple because the LORD had afflicted him.

cards.text: So King Uzziah is a leper until the day of his death, living in isolation, cut off from the house of the LORD. The man who walked in where he had no right to be... now can't walk in at all.

cards.question: With King Uzziah living in isolation, who has charge of the royal palace and governs the people of the land?

cards.text: The rest of Uzziah's acts, from beginning to end, were recorded by the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz. That's a big name keeping your records, friend.

cards.question: Uzziah is buried near his fathers in a field of burial that belonged to the kings, for the people said, "He was a ___."

cards.text: And his son Jotham reigns in his place. Friend, all those towers, and not one of them could keep the pride out.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 16 quotes "He was a ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke 'I've sat in junk drawers longer than this man has been alive' adds two new facts to his backstory. It says he spent more than sixteen years in the drawer, and it says 'junk drawers,' plural, when his story has one junk drawer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The setup 'sits on the throne in Jerusalem a long time' rules out the wrong answer 'twelve' before the baker picks.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The cards go out of order. Card 2 asks about verse 3, then card 3 goes back to tell verse 2. The walkthrough moves backward instead of forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The army stretch (vv. 11-14) goes item by item: the exact counts of 2,600 and 307,500, and every piece of equipment. The building and army stretch (vv. 9-14) is also split across two summary cards, 13 and 14.

rule.text: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card. ... He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

findings.problem: 'According to the text, how does he get so powerful?' sounds like a test question, not Papa Dorin pausing mid-story.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: The joke 'when eighty priests tell you to put it down' makes the priests' words something the text doesn't say. In verse 18 they tell him to leave the sanctuary, not to put down the censer. Their command to leave is never told on any card.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.
